relations.justification: Logic is the instrument metaphysical argument is conducted with, which is why it is taught first even though it is listed last.
The scientific method and the treatment of measurement uncertainty are two halves of what makes an experimental claim checkable.
The historical record of paradigm change refutes a purely cumulative account of confirmation, which is why falsification and paradigm accounts remain in tension.
Replication requires a protocol detailed enough for an independent party to repeat the work; an unreproducible method makes the claim unfalsifiable in practice.
Source evaluation applies the epistemic criteria the philosophy of science articulates.
Morphological analysis segments forms whose boundaries phonology establishes.
The comparative method rests on regular sound correspondence, which is a phonological observation.
Morphological typology exemplifies a coding trade-off: agglutinating languages spend morphemes where isolating ones spend word order.
Syntax combines words whose internal structure morphology describes.
Formal grammars and programming-language syntax are the same theory; Chomsky hierarchy and parser design are one literature.
Compositional semantics is defined over syntactic structure; the meaning of a complex expression is computed on its parse.
Sociolinguistic meaning is meaning; the semantic and pragmatic apparatus is prior to its social distribution.
Lexical semantics generalises what a thesaurus encodes: sense relations are the theory a controlled vocabulary implements.
Regular sound change is the mechanism by which a speech community's varieties become distinct languages.
The comparative method and phylogenetic reconstruction are one inferential procedure: shared innovations imply common ancestry in both.
Sustained contact produces convergence that obscures genealogical relationship, which is why family assignment is contested at the margins.
Sociolinguistic variation is social stratification observed in language.
The poverty-of-stimulus argument refutes purely behaviourist accounts of language learning, which is why learning theory in education cannot be applied to grammar acquisition unmodified.
Poetic devices are described against the genre conventions that give them effect.
Literary theory argues about what the devices do; the devices are prior to the argument.
Close reading is the application of the craft vocabulary; without it the reading has nothing to name.
Formalist and structuralist criticism borrow their analytic apparatus directly from linguistics.
Formalism locates meaning in the text and reader-response locates it in the reading; the two cannot both be the whole account.
Philosophy of religion is philosophy applied to a specific domain of claims.
Active-audience accounts of popular culture contradict the passive-reception model that mass-society media sociology assumed.
The Western genre system — epic, tragedy, comedy, lyric — was codified in classical literature and inherited from it.
Modern argumentation theory derives from classical rhetoric and retains its categories.
Framing research derives from media sociology and its account of symbolic production.
